transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 53 minutes (approx)
Recorders: Fireflies automated transcript
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Lee (Vela PM), Marta Ruiz (Vela ML Eng), Samir Patel (Vela Security), Riley Chen (Vela Ops)
Links shared: deck - https://redwood.ai/decks/vela-quality-pulse, pilot template - https://redwood.ai/pilot/vela, quickstart notebook - https://redwood.ai/quickstarts/console-notebook

Summary:
Quick demo of Redwood "Quality Pulse" workflow (prompt sets + regression alerts + A/B / split comparisons) oriented to Vela Retail's product-search assistant. Focus on how Console + API + Optimize can detect regressions after model upgrades or prompt changes and enable split testing traffic routes. Customer wants a 1-week pilot to validate improvements and cost/latency targets; security questions around SOC2 and VPC onboarding.

Topics covered:
- Prompt set design for e-comm search and classification
- Regression alert thresholds and alerting hooks (PagerDuty, Slack)
- A/B comparisons and statistical test support in Console
- Traffic split routing (hosted vs dedicated, and private VPC considerations)
- Pilot scope, success metrics (NDCG / CTR / latency), and timeline

Action recap (at end): see Action Items and Next Steps above.

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, auto-generated, some transcription artifacts)
[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the Vela account, Priya is our SE. We got about 50 minutes. Sound good?
[00:00:14] Jordan (Vela): Yep, thanks Alex, excited. We have Marta and Samir here — quick context: we run a conversational search assistant for shopping, looking to reduce bad search hits after rolling model updates. Main ask: how do you catch regressions and prove A/B wins?
[00:00:36] Priya (SE): Great, that's exactly what Quality Pulse and the split-test tools are built for. We'll show prompt sets, the regression alerting workflow, and how to run an A/B split using the Console and the API. I'll toggle to the demo deck first.
[00:00:55] Marta (Vela): Just to flag — we have very bursty traffic at 11am PST, and latency SLO is 250ms p50, 600ms p95. Also we use a private VPC currently for inference.
[00:01:10] Priya (SE): Got it. We'll show both hosted and dedicated flows and how the routing policy can pin to dedicated or fallback to hosted. Note: private VPC onboarding is supported but there's some lead time for network peering.
[00:01:26] Liam (Solutions): Quick plug — Optimize can recommend quant profiles to meet latency targets while keeping quality stable; we'll demo that later.
[00:01:40] Samir (Security): Two quick things: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, and KMS integration — do you have certs and docs?
[00:01:50] Alex (AE): Yes, we'll share the security package after — Priya, anything to add?
[00:01:55] Priya (SE): We'll put the SOC2 PDF and our KMS/HSM integration notes in the follow-up. For the demo: opening the Console — sorry, screen is a bit laggy.
[00:02:10] [screen share starts]
[00:02:20] Priya (SE): This is the Quality Pulse dashboard. Top-left you see a quick metric set: NDCG, top-k accuracy, and a drift score. Under that, the Prompt Sets panel — you define multiple prompt sets that represent typical user intents, e.g., 'search exact sku', 'size guidance', 'styling advice'.
[00:02:44] Jordan (Vela): Can we map metrics to our business KPIs? We care about CTR lift and product add-to-cart not just NDCG.
[00:02:53] Priya (SE): Absolutely — you can customize evaluators and map them to your KPIs; Console supports ingestion of offline labels and online telemetry. For CTR/ATC we can ingest your event stream — there's a connector template in the quickstart.
[00:03:10] Marta (Vela): How do we create prompt sets? We have hundreds of intents and seasonal variations.
[00:03:18] Priya (SE): You can import CSVs or use the API to create prompt sets. In the example I'm loading, we have three prompt sets: baseline-search, size-guidance, fallback-fixes. Each has a small evaluation harness with expected outputs and a golden label.
[00:03:40] [00:03:40] Priya (SE): Note: sometimes the auto-transcript shows KV cash instead of KV cache — ignore that, it's a known transcription glitch.
[00:03:50] Riley (Vela): For A/B splits, how do you route live traffic? Do we need to change our client?
[00:03:58] Priya (SE): Minimal changes. You can route at Redwood's ingress by adding a header to your API call or configuring routing rules in the Console by path/percentage. This supports gradual rollouts, canary, and deterministic bucketing.
[00:04:15] Jordan (Vela): And can we compare two different model versions plus prompt variants in the same split?
[00:04:23] Priya (SE): Yes — you can define variants that include model version, prompt set, quantization profile, and routing policies. The A/B comparator will show per-variant metrics and run statistical significance tests.
[00:04:40] Marta (Vela): What statistical tests? We need to be careful with low-frequency intents.
[00:04:47] Priya (SE): We use bootstrap CIs by default and also support t-tests and Bayesian uplift estimates. For low-frequency events we recommend augmenting with offline evaluation using your labeled prompt sets.
[00:05:05] Samir (Security): On data residency: Vela requires EU user interaction data to stay in region. How does Redwood handle that?
[00:05:12] Alex (AE): We support region pinning and private deployments that keep inference in customer-controlled VPCs. We'll add a note for your legal team.
[00:05:22] [00:05:22] Priya (SE): Back to the demo — here's a sample regression alert rule. You can set an alert when NDCG drops by more than 3% week-over-week for a prompt set, or when p95 latency increases by X ms. Alerts can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or create a ticket via webhook.
[00:05:44] Jordan (Vela): Do alerts include example transcripts where the model regressed?
[00:05:49] Priya (SE): Yes, the alert payload includes a small slice of failing requests with the input, model output, and expected label if available. It's helpful for triage.
[00:05:59] Marta (Vela): Nice. How easy is it to run pairwise comparisons? We want to know which prompt tweak caused a regression.
[00:06:08] Priya (SE): There's an AB/Pairwise view — you can run pairwise diffs across prompt sets and model versions. It shows per-example differences and aggregate metrics. Also supports stratification by user segment.
[00:06:24] [00:06:24] Liam (Solutions): Quick note — the optimize engine will surface candidates that trade token cost vs quality. It can recommend a 4-bit quant model plus caching settings to hit your p95 target.
[00:06:37] Riley (Vela): Caching settings — you mean prefix cache? We have a mix of short queries and multi-step sessions.
[00:06:45] Priya (SE): Yes, prefix caching plus KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash in notes) for multi-turn. You can set TTLs per prompt set. For short queries we use aggressive batching with lower wait windows to maintain latency.
[00:07:05] Samir (Security): About private deployment — are audit logs available? We need immutable logs for our auditors.
[00:07:12] Alex (AE): Yes, Private includes audit logging and optional log forwarding to your SIEM. We'll include retention policy options in the security package.
[00:07:25] Jordan (Vela): Walk me through a concrete pilot plan — what do we need to send you?
[00:07:33] Priya (SE): For a 1-week pilot we need: 1) sample traffic routing (we can mirror a percent of traffic), 2) three prompt sets representative of your high-volume intents, 3) your KPIs and an event stream connector (or a sample CSV), and 4) approval for a dedicated test env if you want pinned capacity.
[00:07:55] Marta (Vela): We can provide the prompt sets and a traffic CSV. What's the expected cost model for a week of dedicated test capacity?
[00:08:05] Alex (AE): We'll send a pilot pricing spreadsheet. Roughly it's a short-term reserved node with burst capacity; price depends on model size and expected token volume. We'll include hosted fallback pricing for comparison.
[00:08:20] [00:08:20] Priya (SE): Now I'll demo a quick live A/B run — creating two variants: Variant A (current model + baseline prompts), Variant B (new model quantized + prompt tweaks).
[00:08:35] [00:08:35] Priya (SE): Setting traffic split 70/30, enabling drift monitoring and regression alerts. There's an option to auto-roll back if a safety metric fails — useful for sensitive flows.
[00:08:52] Marta (Vela): How fast does the rollback happen? We need less than 2 minutes SLA for rollback actions.
[00:08:59] Priya (SE): Rollback is near-instant once the rule triggers, typically within 30–90 seconds, depending on in-flight requests. We can tune that.
[00:09:10] Jordan (Vela): For our offline evals, can we run the same comparator on historic logs?
[00:09:17] Priya (SE): Yes, Console supports backfill evaluations — you can run the A/B comparator on historical requests or on your labeled test set to estimate lift before rolling out.
[00:09:30] Riley (Vela): Any limits on history size? We have several terabytes of logs.
[00:09:35] Liam (Solutions): We don't need to ingest terabytes — you can sample or provide a shard. For pilot, a representative sample is fine. For production we provide ingestion pipelines and retention policies.
[00:09:48] [00:09:48] Samir (Security): On SSO and RBAC — can we map roles to our internal groups? We want least privilege for ML engineers vs ops.
[00:09:56] Alex (AE): Yes, SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We'll provide mapping examples in the security docs.
[00:10:10] Priya (SE): Now I'll show the pairwise diff UI — here's an example from another retail customer where a prompt tweak decreased recall on 'size guidance' but increased precision on 'sku match'. The pairwise shows the exact inputs where outputs diverged and a delta chart.
[00:10:34] Jordan (Vela): Very helpful. Do you keep example buckets for manual review? Our CS team wants a triage queue.
[00:10:42] Priya (SE): Yes — failing examples can be pushed to a triage queue in Console, annotated, and assigned to owners. You can also export for offline review.
[00:10:55] Marta (Vela): Can we run automated labeling workflows? A lot of our intents need human-in-the-loop labels.
[00:11:02] Priya (SE): There's a labeling integration; you can route samples to your labeling provider or use Redwood's lightweight annotator UI.
[00:11:12] [00:11:12] Jordan (Vela): For the A/B stats, how does multiple comparisons correction work? We run dozens of prompt experiments.
[00:11:20] Priya (SE): We provide Benjamini-Hochberg FDR corrections and also per-family correction settings. You can group experiments by prompt family.
[00:11:35] Riley (Vela): Does the Console produce a PDF report for stakeholders? Our execs want a one-pager.
[00:11:41] Priya (SE): Yes — exportable executive summaries with key metrics and example diffs.
[00:11:50] [00:11:50] Jordan (Vela): Let's talk about telemetry. We need token-level cost breakdowns aligned with experiments.
[00:11:57] Liam (Solutions): Token-level cost is available in the billing view; Experiment-level cost allocation is surfaced in the Console so you can see cost per variant and per prompt set. Optimize can recommend cost-saving levers.
[00:12:12] Marta (Vela): Any limitations on model families? We mostly use open models but also evaluate some hosted proprietary ones.
[00:12:19] Priya (SE): Platform supports many open and closed models; for proprietary models we can run connectors or let you bring-your-own-model in private deployment.
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Samir (Security): For private deployment, what's the expected provisioning time? We need an on-prem option for some EU data.
[00:12:37] Alex (AE): Private VPC provisioning typically 4–6 weeks depending on network setup; on-prem packages can take longer. We'll scope timeline in the pilot doc.
[00:12:50] Jordan (Vela): On the API side, what's the latency overhead vs direct model hosting?
[00:12:56] Priya (SE): Overhead is minimal; most latency is model inference. With dedicated pinned nodes and quantization/caching we can meet your p95 targets. We'll run a benchmark during the pilot.
[00:13:12] [00:13:12] Priya (SE): Demo: show a regression alert triggered — notice it includes sample failing requests and a comparison to baseline. I'll open the pairwise panel: see the divergent examples.
[00:13:32] Marta (Vela): The output for one input shows tokenization oddities — is that model-specific?
[00:13:38] Priya (SE): Could be tokenization or prompt formatting; pairwise helps isolate whether it's model choice or prompt phrasing.
[00:13:50] Riley (Vela): For the pilot, can you mirror traffic rather than full split? We prefer dark-launching.
[00:13:58] Priya (SE): Mirror mode is supported — you can mirror 10% to Redwood for scoring without impacting users, then compare offline.
[00:14:10] Jordan (Vela): Great. Regarding the statistical reporting window, can we set rolling windows or compare fixed epochs?
[00:14:18] Priya (SE): Both — rolling windows, fixed epoch comparisons, and cohort stratification are supported.
[00:14:30] [00:14:30] Alex (AE): I want to check in on success criteria — Jordan, what would a successful pilot look like?
[00:14:36] Jordan (Vela): We want to see no >2% drop in NDCG across top 10 intents, an uptick in CTR for recommended products by 1.5%, and p95 latency under 600ms. Also verify alerting and the rollback workflow.
[00:14:52] Alex (AE): Perfect, we'll bake those into the pilot acceptance criteria.
[00:14:58] Marta (Vela): Who will be our day-to-day contact during the pilot?
[00:15:04] Alex (AE): Priya will be primary SE contact, and Liam will help on Optimize and ops.
[00:15:12] [00:15:12] Priya (SE): Demo wrap-up: I'll export the comparator results and attach a sample report. Now quick Q&A.
[00:15:28] Samir (Security): Another security Q: do you cache any raw PII or can we mask tokens?
[00:15:36] Priya (SE): We support redaction and token masking at the ingestion layer; KV cache does not persist PII when configured to scrub. We'll include config examples.
[00:15:50] Riley (Vela): If we pin to dedicated capacity, can we burst across regions?
[00:15:57] Liam (Solutions): We support cross-region fallback; routing policies can prefer a region and fallback to nearest healthy region.
[00:16:08] Jordan (Vela): Ok, next practicals — timeline and deliverables?
[00:16:13] Alex (AE): Proposed: Kickoff next Monday (2027-02-07), 1-week pilot, mid-week benchmark run, final review on 2027-02-14. We'll send calendar invites.
[00:16:25] Marta (Vela): That works. Any blockers?
[00:16:29] Samir (Security): Need to vet the security package first; if okay we'll proceed with VPC peering.
[00:16:36] Alex (AE): Understood — we'll email the security artifacts and a short readme for the legal team.

[00:16:55] [00:16:55] Jordan (Vela): Great, thanks. Any final questions?
[00:17:00] Marta (Vela): One more — reporting cadence during pilot? Daily lightweight telemetry and a mid-week deep-dive?
[00:17:07] Alex (AE): Yes, daily check-ins (10–15 min) and a mid-week 45-min bench review. We'll schedule those.

[00:17:30] Alex (AE): Thanks everyone. Meeting ends.
